街の食堂、屋台、出前アプリまで。辛さの調整も、食べきれない分の持ち帰りも、ひと言: From neighborhood diners and street stalls to delivery apps. Ask for it less spicy, take home what you can't finish: get exactly what you want with just a few words.
北京に赴任して二週間の山田さん。昼休み、会社の近くにある地元の人で賑わう小さな四: Misaki Yamada has been posted to Beijing for two weeks. On her lunch break, she works up the courage to walk alone into a small Sichuan diner near her office, packed with locals. Orders are being shouted back and forth, and there's a QR code on the wall. A young waiter, Xiao Zhang, comes over right away.
食堂の店員、二十歳くらい。声が大きくて元気、口は早いけど面倒見がいい: Waiter at the diner, around twenty. Loud and energetic, a fast talker, but looks out for his customers
北京に赴任した日本人会社員、二十六歳。辛い物は少し苦手: Japanese office worker posted to Beijing, 26. Not great with spicy food
大衆食堂の店員とお客さん。中国の食堂では店員もお客さんもかなりカジュアルで、敬語: A waiter and a customer at a casual diner. In Chinese diners, both staff and customers are very casual, and hardly any polite language is used. Calling out 「服务员！」 loudly is normal. Speaking in short, snappy phrases actually comes across well.
「几位」は人数を丁寧に聞く言い方（「几个人」より丁寧）。答えは「一位」「两位」。: 「几位」 is the polite way to ask how many people (more polite than 「几个人」). The answer is 「一位」, 「两位」, etc. Be careful if you show the number with your fingers: Chinese hand signs for numbers six and up may differ from what you're used to. Six, for example, is shown with the thumb and little finger extended.
こちらへどうぞ。メニュー見ます？ それともQRコードで注文します？: Sit over here. Do you want a menu? Or order by scanning the code?
最近の中国ではテーブルのQRコードを読み取ってスマホで注文する「扫码点餐」が主流: These days in China, the norm is 「扫码点餐」: scanning the QR code on the table and ordering on your phone. But photos alone often don't tell you much, so until you're used to it, it's a good idea to ask for a menu and ask the staff.
メニューを見たいです。何かおすすめはありますか。: I'd like to see the menu. Do you have any recommendations?
うちは宮保鶏丁（鶏肉とピーナッツの炒め）と麻婆豆腐がどっちもおいしいですよ。: Our kung pao chicken and mapo tofu are both really good.
「辣」là は第四声。短く強く下げます。本場の麻婆豆腐は日本のものよりずっと辛く: 「辣」 là is fourth tone: short, strong and falling. Authentic mapo tofu is much spicier than versions often served abroad, and the numbing 「麻」 of Sichuan pepper is intense too. If you can't handle spicy food, always check before ordering.
ちょっと辛いですね。辛さ控えめにもできますよ。: It's a bit spicy. We can make it mild.
辛さはたいてい「微辣」（ピリ辛）、「中辣」、「特辣」の段階で調整できます。ただし: Spiciness can usually be adjusted in steps: 「微辣」 (mild), 「中辣」 (medium) and 「特辣」 (extra hot). But at a Sichuan restaurant, "mild" can still be plenty spicy for many foreigners. You can also ask for 「不要辣」 (not spicy).
じゃあ、ピリ辛の麻婆豆腐を一つと、それからご飯を一杯ください。: Then one mild mapo tofu, and a bowl of rice as well.
中国語の「饭」は「食事」全般を指すことが多いので、白いご飯は「米饭」とはっきり言: In Chinese, 「饭」 often refers to meals in general, so say 「米饭」 clearly for plain white rice. In northern diners, rice doesn't come automatically, so don't forget to order it.
中国ではお冷やの代わりに温かいお湯（热水）や白湯を飲む習慣があります。冷たい飲み: In China, it's customary to drink warm or hot water (「热水」) rather than iced water. If you want something cold, you need to say 「要冰的」, or you may get room-temperature beer.
以上です。あ、麻婆豆腐にパクチーは入れないでください。: No, that's all. Oh, no cilantro in the mapo tofu, please.
パクチー（香菜）は中国料理にとてもよく入っています。苦手なものは「不要放〜」で伝: Cilantro (「香菜」) goes into a great many Chinese dishes. To say what you don't want, 「不要放...」 is all you need. If you have an allergy, say so clearly, as in 「我对花生过敏」 ("I'm allergic to peanuts").
はいよ、すぐお持ちします！: You got it, coming right up!
店員を「服务员」と大きな声で呼ぶのは失礼ではありません。気になるなら「你好」でも: Calling out 「服务员」 loudly to the staff isn't rude. If it bothers you, you can also get their attention with 「你好」. Besides 「买单」 mǎidān, you can also say 「结账」.
全部で三十八元です。壁のQRコードを読み取ってください。: That's 38 yuan altogether. There's a QR code on the wall; just scan it.
「看一下菜单」＝メニューを見る。紙のメニューがない店では「有菜单吗？」と聞いてみ: 「看一下菜单」 = to look at the menu. At places without a paper menu, try asking 「有菜单吗？」
「有什么推荐的？」＝おすすめは？ 看板料理は「招牌菜」: 「有什么推荐的？」 = "What do you recommend?" A house specialty is a 「招牌菜」
「不辣」「微辣」「特辣」で調整。「麻辣」はしびれる辛さ: Adjust with 「不辣」, 「微辣」 and 「特辣」. 「麻辣」 is numbing and spicy
四川や湖南の店の「微辣」は手ごわい。不安なら「一点点辣」と念を押す: "Mild" at a Sichuan or Hunan restaurant can be a challenge. If you're worried, stress it with 「一点点辣」
「一碗米饭」＝ご飯一杯。北方では麺や「馒头」（蒸しパン）が主食のことも: 「一碗米饭」 = a bowl of rice. In the north, noodles or 「馒头」 (steamed buns) are often the staple instead
w:碗|〜杯（お碗に入ったものを数える）: bowl; (measure word) for things served in a bowl
「一碗米饭」「一碗面」。「碗」はお碗そのものの意味もある: 「一碗米饭」, 「一碗面」. 「碗」 also means the bowl itself
中国では体を冷やさないよう温かい水を飲むのが一般的: In China, people generally drink warm water so as not to chill the body
「免费的吗？」＝無料ですか。お茶や漬物が無料の店も多い: 「免费的吗？」 = "Is it free?" Many places serve tea or pickles for free
「不要放香菜」は旅行者が最初に覚えるべきフレーズの一つ: 「不要放香菜」 is one of the first phrases travelers should learn
店員を呼ぶときの呼びかけ。大きな声で呼んでOK: Used to call the staff. It's fine to call out loudly
w:买单|お会計（する）: to pay the bill; check, please
「结账」も同じ意味。食堂では先払いの店もある: 「结账」 means the same. Some diners have you pay up front
「扫二维码」＝QRコードを読み取る。会話では単に「码」とも言う: 「扫二维码」 = to scan a QR code. In conversation, often just 「码」
w:打包|持ち帰り用に包む: to pack up (food) to take away
「这个打包」＝これ包んでください。残った料理の持ち帰りはごく普通: 「这个打包」 = "Please pack this up." Taking leftovers home is completely normal
形容詞・動詞の肯定形 + 不 + 否定形: adjective / verb in the affirmative + 不 + negative
「辣吗？」と同じ意味ですが、「辣不辣？」の方が口語的で、答えを素直に聞いている感: It means the same as 「辣吗？」, but 「辣不辣？」 is more colloquial and gives the feeling of simply asking for an honest answer. If you ask 「好吃不好吃？」 or 「贵不贵？」 at a diner, the staff will answer casually and honestly. Don't put 「吗」 at the end.
苦手な食材や体に合わないものを伝える基本形。日本人は「できれば……」と遠回しに言: The basic way to say what ingredients you dislike or can't eat. Learners often hedge with something like "if possible...," but Chinese kitchens are busy, so saying it briefly and clearly is the surest way to get the message across. Being direct isn't rude.
塩は少なめにしてください。: Go easy on the salt, please.
注文を続けるとき、追加するときの言い方。「再」は「さらに、もう一度」。「再要一碗: How to keep ordering or add something to your order. 「再」 means "additionally, once more." 「再要一碗米饭」 also works for asking for another bowl of rice. You don't have to say everything at once: just add things with 「再要...」 as they come to mind, which takes the pressure off.
街の食堂、ファストフード、フードコートなど気軽なお店全般。人数→注文→苦手なもの: Neighborhood diners, fast food, food courts and casual places in general. Once you know the flow (number of people, ordering, what you don't eat, paying), you can walk in confidently even on your own.
日本の感覚で店員が来るまで黙って待っていると、ずっと放っておかれることも。また「: If you sit quietly waiting for the staff to come over, you may be ignored indefinitely. And if you're vague, saying something like "spicy is a bit...," they'll assume you're fine with it and bring it at normal spiciness. Say clearly at the start what you can't eat.
店員さんは忙しいので、はっきり短く言ってくれるお客さんはむしろありがたい存在です: Staff are busy, so customers who speak briefly and clearly are actually appreciated. When a foreigner makes an effort to order in Chinese, staff may even come by to check, "Not too spicy?"
中国の食堂は、とにかく賑やかです。大声の注文、厨房に響く鍋の音、店員同士の掛け合: Chinese diners are loud, no matter what. Orders shouted out, woks clanging in the kitchen, staff calling back and forth. Even if the language sounds rough, nobody's angry; it's a sign of a lively place with good food. When you finish eating, do try telling the staff or the kitchen 「很好吃！」. Nothing makes the cooks happier. Taking home food you couldn't finish (「打包」) is also welcomed as a good habit that values food. If the next time you go they remember, "Mild, right?", you're a regular.
店に入ると「几位？」と聞かれました。一人のときの答えは？: When you enter a restaurant, you're asked 「几位？」. How do you answer if you're alone?
人数を聞かれたら「〜位」で答えるのが自然です。「碗」はお碗、「块」はお金の単位で: When asked how many people, it's natural to answer with "...「位」." 「碗」 means bowl, and 「块」 is a unit of money.
白いご飯を頼みたいとき、いちばん確実な言い方は？: What is the surest way to order plain white rice?
「饭」だけだと「食事」全般の意味になりがち。「米饭」とはっきり言い、量詞は「碗」: 「饭」 alone tends to mean meals in general. Say 「米饭」 clearly and use the measure word 「碗」.
パクチーが苦手です。注文のときに何と言えばいい？: You don't like cilantro. What should you say when ordering?
中国では苦手なものは短くはっきり伝えるのが一番。ぼかすと伝わりません。: In China, it's best to say briefly and clearly what you don't eat. Being vague won't get the message across.
食べきれなかった料理を持ち帰りたいときの言葉は？: What do you say when you want to take home food you couldn't finish?
「打包」は残った料理を包んでもらうこと。中国ではごく普通の習慣です。: 「打包」 means having leftover food packed up. It's a completely normal practice in China.

w:想|…したい；考える；恋しく思う: to want to; to think; to miss (someone)
